beats.heading: What was built
beats.narration_text: Two animations in a two-D Godot game: one loops, one commits. And one lesson. A test can prove a clip is built the way the plan says. Only real frames and human eyes can say whether the motion reads.

props.text:
Two animations for a Godot game.
A passing test proves the motion.

beats.heading: The game, the two clips
beats.narration_text: Extinguisho is Sreeja's deadpan ninja firefighter. The cycle: the trapped person in the window waves, one arm turning on a shoulder pivot. The committing action: Joe grabs the survivor, flings them sky-high without looking, and settles back into his stance.

beats.narration_text: Before any clip existed, the brief, written from Sreeja's decisions, named both clips, the route each one takes, the single thing allowed to drive each, and the toss as a table of frames: grab, throw, settle. Behaviour pins came next: tests that record what the game already does, so the change can be checked against them.

beats.heading: A clip is a list of keys
beats.narration_text: First idea: a clip is a list of keys, not a movie. The whole wave is three keys on one property, the shoulder's rotation: zero, nought point four five radians, zero, over twenty-four frames, looping. Nothing in it knows about the game.

beats.heading: The sheet and its slicing
beats.narration_text: The toss uses a sprite sheet. Claude packed Sreeja's twelve Assignment Two poses into a four by three grid, each placed so his feet land on the same point in every cell. The sprite reads the grid by number.

beats.heading: Feel in frames
beats.narration_text: Second idea: feel is designed in frames. At sixty frames a second, one per physics tick: grab on frame zero, throw from fourteen, settle from thirty, done at forty-six. This script builds the keys from that table; nobody types them by hand.

props.title: Feel in frames
props.source: Godot editor reconstruction · exact source, revision 7848c6e · next: the visible result

const FPS := 60.0                # the phase table's frame rate: one frame per physics tick
const TRACK := "Sprite:frame"    # relative to the AnimationPlayer's root_node, the Art root
# One-key hold clips, one per state the state machine can show outside the toss.
const HOLDS := ["idle", "respawn", "run", "rising", "falling", "landing", "hose", "burned", "celebrate"]
# The toss: [first frame of the phase, cell shown], then the clip length in frames.
const TOSS_KEYS := [[0, "grab"], [14, "toss"], [30, "respawn"]]
const TOSS_FRAMES := 46

beats.heading: A wrong name fails silently
beats.narration_text: Third idea: a track names a node and a property. Misspell the property and Godot stays silent: the clip plays, and nothing moves. So this helper walks every track and checks that its node and property really exist.

beats.heading: What the read-backs caught
beats.narration_text: Both read-backs pass, sixty-six checks on Joe's clips and thirteen on the wave. Then one letter was added to a property name, in a throwaway copy. The test failed and named it. Four other planted mistakes failed their tests too.

beats.heading: One authority
beats.narration_text: Fourth idea: one authority. Only Joe's animation player writes his picture. The state machine just asks it to play a clip, and restarts the toss from frame zero on every grab.

props.title: One authority
props.source: Godot editor reconstruction · exact source, revision 7848c6e · next: the visible result
props.code:
func show_pose(state: String) -> void:
	var clip: String = STATE_CLIPS[state]
	if clip != anim.assigned_animation or (state == "grab" and pose != "grab"):
		anim.play(clip)
		anim.seek(0.0, true)
		clip_started_frame = Engine.get_physics_frames()
	pose = state
	art.scale = Vector2(0.5 * facing, 0.5)
	queue_redraw()  # the bag follows the art

notes.label: Line 89
notes.value: restart on a new clip, or on every grab

beats.heading: The toss in play, interrupted
beats.narration_text: Here, a jump interrupts the grab on frame seven. The toss carries on in the air: moving never cancels it. Had a second writer touched the frame, the last one to run would win. A planted one failed the state test.

beats.heading: Two clocks
beats.narration_text: And two clocks. The game launches the survivor on the physics tick, so Joe's clip advances by hand on that same tick, and only while he's enabled.

props.title: Two clocks
props.source: Godot editor reconstruction · exact source, revision 7848c6e · next: the visible result
props.code:
move_and_slide()
	position.x = maxf(position.x, 10.0)
	_update_pose()
	# The clips' clock (CHANGE-BRIEF "The two clocks"): one physics tick of clip time per tick while
	# enabled, so pause, dying and complete freeze the clip as they freeze the action queue. A clip
	# (re)started on this tick stays on its frame 0.
	if Engine.get_physics_frames() != clip_started_frame:
		anim.advance(delta)
	queue_redraw()

notes.label: Line 193

beats.heading: Pause and restart
beats.narration_text: So pause freezes the toss on its frame and resumes it from there, and R cuts it with the respawn stance. The throw now lands exactly on the launch tick. Before, the picture was two ticks late, about three hundredths of a second.

beats.heading: What the pins caught
beats.narration_text: The pins paid off before a single key existed. The brief said the launch came on frame fifteen. The pin measured fourteen. Claude had read the code and was off by one, the exact failure the brief predicted. The table moved; the keys followed. The pins also caught an old bug: R at a rescued window rescues them again. Recorded, not fixed.

beats.heading: What Claude got wrong
beats.narration_text: The agent's recorded mistakes: that off-by-one, two bugs in its own tests caught before commit, and four commands its read-only session tried and was refused. And the limit stays: no headless run draws a pixel. Whether the motion reads is Sreeja's call, in the running game.

beats.heading: Verdict
beats.narration_text: The verdict. Verified by tests: both clips built as the brief says, the pins unchanged, every state, every interrupt, and every planted mistake caught. Still to come: Sreeja's own eye checks in the running game. Next step: guard the rescue against that old re-rescue. Directed and decided by Sreeja, implemented by Claude. The sheet is her own Assignment Two art; OpenAI's terms give her the rights.
